name: ActionSheet
abstract: An action drawer attached to a caller-owned trigger.
discussion:
The sheet is one bottom drawer at every width: compact surfaces get a
full-width panel with a drag handle and no close control; wider surfaces
get a centered, bounded drawer with a top close control. The caller owns
the visible labels and supplies the localized accessibility name for that
close control, so the component never writes interface copy such as
"Cancel" or "Close" itself.

name: CommandItem
abstract: One entry in a `CommandPalette`.
discussion:
`keywords` are the search-only aliases nobody sees — the abbreviation, the
old name, the menu path. Without them a palette only finds commands whose
title the user already remembers, which is exactly when they do not need one.

members.name: group

name: CommandPalette
abstract: Searchable command surface presented as a modal overlay.
discussion:
A palette is worth more than the menu it replaces only if finding a command
is faster than looking for it, so ranking is deliberately aggressive: a
title prefix outranks a word start, which outranks a substring, which
outranks a subsequence match. Typing three letters should put the intended
command first without requiring the exact wording.

Keyboard is the primary path — arrows move, Return runs, Escape closes — and
the search field keeps focus throughout, so the hands never leave the
keyboard.

name: Popover
declaration: public struct Popover<Label: View, Content: View>: View
abstract: Overlay opened by a labelled trigger button. Touch surfaces use a bottom sheet; pointer surfaces anchor the overlay to its trigger.
discussion:
The popup is portal-rendered, so it escapes any clipping or stacking
context the trigger sits in, and it is dismissed by Escape, by losing the
pointer, or by the trigger being pressed again.

`Popover` owns the trigger button. Surfaces that need a different trigger
(a hover card, a context menu) use `AnchoredOverlayHost` directly.

name: PortalStore
abstract: Per-window store of overlay (popover/menu/tooltip) entries.
discussion:
Phase 3 (坏味 #3): the storage moved off `PortalRegistry`'s process-global
`enum` statics into this instance so each window owns its own overlay layer —
one window's open dropdown can never paint into, or swallow clicks for,
another's. Phase 8 deleted the legacy `PortalRegistry` static shim: call
sites read `PortalStoreHolder.current` (the scoped ambient swapped by
`withCurrent`) and entry owners remember their store for cleanup.

name: TooltipArbitration
abstract: Window-wide tooltip rules, matching mygo's engine: one tip at a time, the innermost target wins, and a tip that follows another within the warm window skips the rest delay so the pointer can travel along a toolbar.
discussion:
Owned by the window's `PlatformInputContext`, like the portal store (规则 3):
two windows must not take tips from each other, and a fresh context starts
with none on screen. The holder is empty until a window registers one, so a
bare tree (previews, tests that do not care) simply has no arbitration and
every tip times out on its own.

Main-thread-only, like the portal store: tooltips are presented and
dismissed on the UI thread.

name: TooltipArbitrationAmbient
abstract: Registers a window's tooltip rules for as long as its input context is current, mirroring `PortalStoreAmbient`.
